nodes.label: ADR001: Select ADR Templates Based on Configured UI Language
nodes.rationale: Chosen to keep ADR content consistent with the rest of the localized experience (UI strings) instead of leaving templates mismatched, and to avoid the complexity/unreliability of on-demand runtime translation. Trade-off: the 9 new language template variants are machine-translated and pending native-speaker review.
nodes.norm_label: adr001: select adr templates based on configured ui language

nodes.label: ADR002: Add a Plugin System for ADR Lifecycle Event Integrations
nodes.rationale: Chosen design: a single, non-retried, timeout-bounded dispatch inline in the foreground, with full retry only during a separate background re-drive (adrplus sync), so the core stays integration-agnostic (via IAdrPlugin) while keeping interactive commands fast regardless of external-system health. Trade-off: sync with external systems is eventual, not transactional; v1 is local/per-developer rather than CI-authoritative, deferred pending real usage data.
nodes.norm_label: adr002: add a plugin system for adr lifecycle event integrations

nodes.label: ADR003: Store Plugin Binaries Host-Globally Instead of Per-Repository
nodes.rationale: Pivoted away from the original per-repository plugin storage design (D36) because plugin binaries don't need to be duplicated/versioned separately per repository on a machine - only the per-repo activeplugins/disableplugins on/off switch does. Trade-off: a developer must install a plugin once per machine before any repo can activate it; there is no longer a 'clone the repo and you already have the plugin' experience; higher memory footprint from one AssemblyLoadContext per loaded plugin.
nodes.norm_label: adr003: store plugin binaries host-globally instead of per-repository

nodes.label: Host-global plugin storage (%UserProfile%/AdrPlus.Plugins/<name>/)
nodes.rationale: Plugin binaries, manifest, and dependencies are installed once per machine under %UserProfile%/AdrPlus.Plugins/<name>/ rather than per-repository; AdrPlus discovers and loads them automatically, while each repository still controls activation independently via activeplugins/disableplugins in its own adr-config.adrplus (ADR003 pivot from prior per-repo ./plugins/<name>/ model).

nodes.label: Host-global plugin storage (%UserProfile%/AdrPlus.Plugins/<name>/)
nodes.rationale: Installed once per machine under %UserProfile%/AdrPlus.Plugins/<name>/, discovered and loaded automatically; each repository controls activation independently via activeplugins/disableplugins in its own adr-config.adrplus.

nodes.label: Host-global plugin storage (%UserProfile%/AdrPlus.Plugins/<name>/)
nodes.rationale: Plugins are loaded from %UserProfile%/AdrPlus.Plugins/<name>/, installed once per machine and shared across every repository on it, rather than per-repository storage.

nodes.label: Plugin trust model (no sandboxing)
nodes.rationale: Plugins are third-party code that runs with the invoking user's own OS permissions - the same trust level as any other executable the user chooses to run. AdrPlus does not sandbox plugin code.

nodes.label: Credential handling rule for plugin settings
nodes.rationale: Never put real credential values in a plugin's settings block since plugin.json is plain JSON on disk at the host-global location; credential resolution (tokens, API keys) is entirely the plugin's own responsibility, never the host's.
nodes.norm_label: credential handling rule for plugin settings
